newsitem.title: THAILAND: Blue chip Siam Cement tumbles limit down.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip Siam Cement tumbles limit down.

text.p: Siam Cement Plc dropped its 10 percent limit in late trade on Wednesday along with other major blue chips as investors unloaded local stocks on concerns over Thailand's currency and economic slowdown, analysts said.
Siam Cement, Thailand's largest cement manufacturer, was trading down to the limit at 558 baht by 0853 GMT, after falling 62 baht. It was ranked third on the most active list by value.
Despite the heavy selling by foreign investors, some analysts said the stock remained a good long-term investment.
Analysts said investors also sold Siam Cement on worries that its first quarter earnings would not be impressive.
Analysts have said Siam Cement would continue to post a rise in first quarter net profit, but at a slower rate of five to six percent over the same period last year.
In the first quarter of 1996, the firm posted a 20 percent rise in net profit to 2.64 billion baht from 2.19 billion in the same period the year before.

"Siam Cement is still a good buy for an investment in long-term because its building material products are still in great demand for ongoing and future infrastructure projects," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
